title: GitHub Contribution Streak
dataSources: RescueTime activity (`rescuetime:activity`), screen-time exports (`screentime:usage`), GitHub events (`github:personal`), habit-tracker logs (`habit:entry`), calendar exports.
app: Screen-time / RescueTime exports, GitHub personal activity, habit/journal trackers, and calendar feeds via HEC scripted inputs.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=github:personal
| bin _time span=1d
| stats sum(eval(if(type="PushEvent",1,0))) as commits_days by _time
| streamstats current=t sum(eval(if(commits_days>0,1,0))) as streak reset_after="(commits_days=0)"
| sort - _time
description: Recreates your coding contribution streak from GitHub events so you can protect the green squares that keep side projects alive.
value: A visible streak is a proven motivator for hobby coding; recreating it in your own dashboard keeps momentum without opening the site.
implementation: Ingest your GitHub events to HEC; schedule daily and surface your current streak.
visualization: Calendar heatmap of daily contributions with the current streak.
grandmaExplanation: It tracks how many days in a row you have worked on your coding projects, which helps keep the habit going.
